title: Feeling jittery today?
caption: Feeling jittery today? That wired-then-tired swing may pop in—restless, shallow breathing and then a quick dip. Keep tasks short, take brief movement breaks, and try two minutes of slow breathing to steady up before your next step.
snapshot: Geomagnetic readings climbed into the active band. The magnetic field dipped south at times, which often adds variability. Solar wind speed looks ordinary. No flares or CMEs observed.
affects: A wired/tired rhythm may show up as restlessness, shallow breaths, and then a quick fade. Focus windows can feel shorter, with a need to move or step away sooner than usual.
playbook:
- Do 2–3 minutes of slow breathing
- Take brief movement breaks between tasks
- Drink water and keep snacks simple
- Get a few minutes of daylight exposure
- Wind down earlier with softer screens

fb.caption:
Feeling jittery today? Some people may notice a wired-then-tired swing—restless, a bit soda-pop fizz under the skin, breathing stays shallow, and then you hit a quick fade. Focus can come in shorter spurts, with the body asking for a step away sooner than usual.

Environment-wise, geomagnetic readings climbed into the active band, and the magnetic field tilted south at times—conditions that can stir variability even while the solar wind itself looks ordinary. No notable flares or CMEs in the mix today. Try a two- to three-minute slow-breath reset before your next task; it can smooth that chesty flutter and lengthen your focus window. Add brief movement between tasks, sip water, keep snacks simple, and grab a few minutes of daylight to anchor your clock. Gaia Eyes watches the back-and-forth between Earth’s magnetic field and the solar wind so you don’t have to.
